methodology: Public-source evidence review, not an AIS feed. Notices support only their stated location and period. A notice is not a measurement of port-wide congestion. Missing measurements remain null; no score, ranking, forecast or historical change is calculated. Health scores run high-is-good; congestion scores run high-is-bad. Neither is currently verified.

findings: src/data/portData.ts contains 17 hard-coded port records, relative update strings and random synthetic history; these are not verified observations.
The production report contains figures labelled 2026-09-02, whereas the search extraction still showed 2026-08-26. Neither date establishes when the metrics were measured.
Other port detail and comparison pages consume the same unverified data. Their numerical results must not be treated as operational evidence.

A scheduled publisher regenerated the weekly report on 9 September with the same unsupported numerical values relabelled as live data. The public current report and dated edition were corrected to explicit unverified states.

An external Carrgo SEO Agent regenerated the production report on 16 September with unsupported synthetic health scores labelled as live data, while the evidence ledger still recorded every numerical measurement as unknown. The current report, archive and dated URL were corrected on 17 September.
audit.changesSincePrevious: Peel Ports’ current Liverpool index still lists Notice 63/2026; its stated Alfred Lock closure window runs from the 03:52 high-water tide until 13:16 on 18 September. Notice 62/2026’s bridge-closure window ended on 17 September. The Met Office shipping forecast now carries gale warnings for the Irish Sea and Malin, and the inshore forecast carries strong-wind warnings around the Irish Sea and Northern Ireland coasts. These are time-limited operating and weather advisories, not port-wide congestion measurements, so no congestion change is calculated.
